entities.name: Spurius Carvilius Maximus Ruga
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Spurius Carvilius Maximus Ruga was a Roman consul in 234 and 228 BC, playing a significant role in the governance of the Roman Republic. As a freedman, he was also a schoolteacher, reflecting the complexities of social mobility and education during the Classical era.

Ruga's influence extended beyond his political office, as he was a member of the Roman elite who navigated the intricate web of relationships between patrons and clients. His appointment as consul underscores the importance of these connections in shaping the course of Roman history.

Despite his relatively minor status, Ruga's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of education and social mobility in the ancient world.

Spurius Carvilius Maximus Ruga's life and career are a reminder that even the most seemingly minor figures can have a lasting impact on the trajectory of human history.
